To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the 250-GHZ ESR spectrum of CSL in DMPC-DMPS membranes is composed of two components, (ii) one of these components has the same orientation as CSL in DMPC and the other has a distinctly different orientation and dynamics, (iii) the latter component arises from CSL molecules that sense a local, strongly anisotropic environment, and (iv) this anisotropic environment is due to the strong interactions between phosphatidylserines.
the ESR spectra of CSL in DMPC membranes show two spectral components, one of which grows in as the DMPS concentration increases and is indicative of a biaxial local ordering.
the CSL in the mixed DMPC/DMPS bilayers senses a local, biaxial, environment that grows in as the DMPS mole fraction increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular-level understanding of the interaction of cholesterol with DMPS, a model membrane component of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria, in mixed model membranes.
the molecular interactions between the phospholipids and cholesterol.
the dynamics and structure of cholesterol in mixed membranes composed of DMPC and DMPS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CSL is a very sensitive probe of local order in lipid bilayers, which is consistent with the fact that it is a good model of cholesterol.
the ESR spectra of CSL in mixed model membranes composed of DMPC and DMPS show that cholesterol and DMPS do not mix well.
the 250-Ghz ESR spectra of cholestane in mixed model membranes provide a unique window into the molecular interactions in the membrane, which are not accessible by other techniques.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
250-GHz ESR provides an excellent tool for studying the local molecular dynamics and order in model membranes.
the biaxial nature of the ordering is a key factor in the understanding of the dynamics of cholesterol and its interactions with DMPS in the mixed DMPC/DMPS bilayer.
the 250-GHZ spectra provide a powerful new tool in membrane biophysics, with excellent resolution of both ordering and dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
250-GHz ESR can be used to study molecular order and dynamics in membranes, and the results can be interpreted in a quantitative fashion.
a 250-GH ESR study of mixed model membranes, using a spin label that is not a phospholipid, can provide information about both ordering and dynamics in the membranes.
250-GHz ESR spectra can be analyzed with the same tools as those used for 9-GHz spectra, with the added benefit of much better orientational resolution.
